historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case average revenue growth FY2027-36 (~4.0%); none of the historical CAGRs is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+6.9% 3y, +9.3% 5y, total equity FY2022 103,286 / FY2020 81,038 -> FY2025 126,360) diverges by >30% from revenue CAGR (-5.7% 3y, -7.5% 5y, FY2022 63,054 / FY2020 77,867 -> FY2025 52,853). Book growth is NOT compounding: it is equity issuance (US government, Nvidia, SoftBank) and SCIP partner contributions into NCI, while retained earnings fell. Equity CAGR rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs undefined (FY2024 -4.38, FY2025 -0.06). Owner-FCF series (OCF - gross capex - SBC - RSU withholdings - interest income) is negative every year FY2022-FY2025 (reported FCF -9,411 / -14,279 / -15,656 / -4,949 before the SBC and interest deductions), so FCF CAGRs are undefined. TTM to Sep-2026 is the first positive owner-FCF print (~3.0bn) since FY2021, and it depends on partner contributions and customer deposits. SBC is not outgrowing cash flow -- SBC fell from 3,410 (FY2024) to ~2,430 TTM with the 15% headcount cut -- but RSU withholding cash doubled with the share price.

scenario_narratives.base: Partial turnaround. 18A ramps on schedule and carries Intel's own client and server roadmap, DCAI's Xeon supply constraint is worked off, and Foundry losses roughly halve by 2028 but never quite reach breakeven because external volume stays modest relative to the installed base. AMD holds its x86 share gains without taking much more. Revenue compounds ~4%/yr to ~91bn by FY2036, EBITDA margin recovers from ~34% to 44% (still six points below Intel's pre-2021 norm), and net capex settles at 18% of revenue once Brookfield's Arizona SCIP funding runs off. Intel becomes a cash-generative but ordinary IDM with ~15bn of steady-state owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: IDM 2.0 works. 14A wins a major external anchor customer and the reported Microsoft/Amazon engagements convert to volume, making Intel the only Western leading-edge foundry with US-government and Nvidia backing; DCAI rides AI-inference demand for general-purpose compute and the Nvidia joint products. Revenue roughly 2.5x to ~153bn by FY2036 with EBITDA margins back to 50%, funded by sustained 20-21% net capex. Even this case values Intel near today's price at a 10% discount rate, which is the central finding: the market is already pricing something close to the bull outcome.
scenario_narratives.bear: Foundry is a value sink. No external 14A anchor arrives, so 14A is curtailed and 18A/Ohio capacity is stranded; AMD keeps taking x86 share in client and server, Intel has no AI-accelerator position, and the PC slowdown runs past H1-2027. Revenue shrinks for two years and is barely above today's level a decade out; EBITDA margin is pinned at 31-33% by under-absorbed fab cost. Capex is cut to maintenance, which rescues some cash flow, but further dilutive financing (not modelled) would be likely on this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF basis: SBC (incl. RSU withholding cash) fully expensed, share count held flat, interest income outside the unlevered flows, NCI deducted once at book, and capex net of the partner contributions that are matched by that NCI claim. Intel is valued as one consolidated IDM whose scenarios differ chiefly on whether Intel Foundry reaches profitability with external customers. At a 10% WACC even the bull case lands near the current price; the market is paying for a Foundry outcome that our base case does not assume.
key_risks_to_valuation: Foundry external-customer outcome is binary and dominates value: the bull/bear spread is ~5x.
Further dilution: Intel issued ~26% more shares FY2023-Sep 2026; the bear path would likely require more, which the flat share count does not charge.
DOC warrants (241M at $20) become exercisable if Foundry is spun below 51% ownership.
Book NCI may misstate the Arizona SCIP and Mobileye claims (Mobileye at market would be larger; SCIP at its contracted return may be smaller).
Cash tax: US valuation allowance and attributes could keep cash tax below 15% for longer (upside), or GILTI/Pillar Two could lift it (downside).
Cyclicality: PC slowdown through at least H1-2027 and semiconductor inventory cycles make FY2027 the least certain year.
Customer deposits (~1.7bn) and peak SCIP partner contributions flatter the TTM reported FCF used as the year-0 anchor.

data_sources.financials: INTC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q for quarter ended 26-Sep-2026: balance sheet, cash flow, Notes 2-4, liquidity section); INTC_Annual_FY2025.txt (10-K FY2025 cash flow statement and adjusted FCF reconciliation); INTC_Metrics.csv / INTC.duckdb segment KPIs
data_sources.qualitative: INTC_Analysis.json (2026-11, incl. Q3-2026 results and Q4-2026 guidance of 15.0-16.0bn revenue, 37.1% GAAP gross margin)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 5,310M issued and outstanding at 26-Sep-2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet; includes all 132M Escrowed Shares issued to the US government, 66M of them still contingent on Secure Enclave disbursements) plus ~60M RSU/option dilution (Q3-2026 diluted 5,307M vs basic 5,244M weighted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 241M DOC warrants at $20 (exercisable only if Intel ceases to own 51% of Foundry) are excluded as not expected to become exercisable; a Foundry spin would trigger them (~4% dilution, partly offset by $4.8bn strike cash). The Aug-2026 $20bn offering (210.5M sh at $95) is already in the 5,310M; no further non-SBC issuance is modelled although the bear case would plausibly need it.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 26-Sep-2026: share-based compensation add-back 2,432 (FY2025 10-K CF 2,434 less 9M-2025 1,896, plus 9M-2026 1,894 from the Q3-2026 10-Q CF) plus restricted-stock-unit withholdings 1,044 (FY2025 423 less 9M-2025 286, plus 9M-2026 907). Intel publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Withholdings are inflated by the 2026 share-price spike (52-week high 142.35); forward path normalises to 4.8% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.25 for a cyclical IDM -> cost of equity ~10.5%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (2026 notes priced 4.65-6.20%); debt ~14% of EV at the current price -> ~9.7%, rounded to 10.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: foundry/turnaround risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a WACC premium (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost sits inside opex and therefore inside adjusted EBITDA; operating-lease liabilities are excluded from total_debt (treatment B, one charge). Finance-lease / vendor-financed equipment payments (951 in 9M-2026, financing section) are treated as capex and folded into capex_pct_path, as are 'Additions to PP&E' paid through financing (1,618 in 9M-2026).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged ONCE, in the bridge: flows are consolidated, and the 16,642 book NCI at 26-Sep-2026 (Arizona SCIP/Brookfield 14,372; Mobileye 2,129; other 141) is deducted in equity_bridge. Capex is modelled NET of partner contributions and capital-related government incentives, because future Brookfield contributions fund their share of Arizona capex against a matching NCI claim (value-neutral). Ireland SCIP minority was bought out for $14.2bn in Q2-2026 and no longer leaks. Mobileye NCI at book understates its market value -- a known conservative-to-Intel error of ~$1-2/share in the other direction is NOT taken; book is used throughout.
inputs.fx_note: Not applicable: statements and quote both USD.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted (routing: operating company, US, cyclical semiconductor IDM with a minority interest -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (c) NCI, (f) risk once). Not a bank/REIT/holdco; no SOTP because Intel discloses no Foundry balance sheet and the Products/Foundry transfer price is internal -- the Foundry turnaround is instead the axis that separates the three scenarios. First valuation of INTC (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2026E = 9M-2026 actual revenue 46,218 + Q4-2026 guide midpoint 15,500 = 61,718. FY2026E adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, ex restructuring/impairment) ~35%: 9M-2026 operating income 1,182 + restructuring and other 4,294 (incl. Mobileye goodwill impairment) + depreciation 8,933 + amortisation 659 + SBC 1,894 = 16,962 (36.7% of revenue), plus a Q4 ~31% on the 37.1% GAAP gross-margin guide. D&A ~20.7% of revenue (depreciation rising as 18A capacity enters service). REPORTED FCF here is Intel's own 'adjusted FCF' definition, TTM to Sep-2026: OCF 17,472 - gross capex incl. financed additions 15,855 + partner contributions 6,488 + government incentives 774 - finance-lease payments 951 = 7,928; it is flattered by ~1.7bn of customer deposits received Q2-2026 and by peak SCIP partner contributions. Net capex (incl. finance leases) TTM ~15.9% of revenue vs 20.8% FY2025 and 30%+ gross in FY2022-24. Buybacks: none since FY2021 and dividend suspended FY2024; the flat share count is a modelling convention Intel is not funding -- it has instead been a large net ISSUER (4,228M FY2023 -> 5,310M Sep-2026, +26%) to fund the Foundry buildout. Cash taxes: US valuation allowance means domestic losses are not benefited and cash tax runs ~1.1-2.3bn/yr; forward cash rate starts at 15% (non-GAAP guide 11%, US attributes partially shelter) and ramps to 18%, NOT perpetuating the shelter. Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (inventory-heavy manufacturer; plus ~3.3bn of substrate prepayments committed through 2027). Excluded from the bridge (all small or contingent): ~2.7bn Secure Enclave cash due from DOC on release of escrowed shares; pending Classiq acquisition (~1.9bn, cash or shares, H1-2027); Escrowed-Shares derivative liability (its shares are already in the count).

bear.rationale: Foundry fails to land an external 14A customer; 14A is curtailed and Intel retreats toward fab-lite, with stranded 18A/Ohio capacity. AMD pushes x86 share further below 70% in client and server; PC slowdown extends past H1-2027. Revenue flat-to-down for three years and ~64bn by FY2036; EBITDA margin stuck at 31-33% as fixed fab cost is under-absorbed; capex cut to 15% (maintenance) and D&A falls toward it.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +3%: CFO guides PC slowdown through at least H1-2027 (CCPG -5% YoY in Q3-2026) against Xeon demand exceeding supply (DCAI +78% YoY). FY2028-29 +6%: DCAI supply unlocked, 18A Panther Lake/Clearwater Forest mix, modest external Foundry revenue (411m in Q3-2026, from ~30m/qtr in 2025). Fades to 2.5% by FY2036. FY2036 revenue ~91bn, below the FY2021 peak of 79bn in real terms.
base.margin_rationale: 34% FY2027 reflects the Q4-2026 gross-margin guide of 37.1% GAAP (node-transition and underutilisation costs). Rising to 44% by FY2032 as Foundry losses (-10.3bn FY2025, ~-7.5bn FY2026 run-rate, -1.85bn in Q3-2026) narrow toward, but do not fully reach, breakeven, and AMD keeps pressure on x86 pricing. Pre-2021 Intel ran ~50%.
base.capex_rationale: NET capex (gross + financed additions + finance leases - partner contributions - government incentives). Rises from ~16% TTM to 18-19% as Arizona SCIP partner funding tapers and 14A tooling starts; 18% steady state equals terminal D&A, i.e. maintenance plus growth at 2.5%. D&A stays ~20% near term (2022-24 gross capex of 24-26bn/yr still depreciating) and converges on capex.

bull.rationale: Foundry wins: 14A secures a major external anchor customer (Microsoft/Amazon design wins convert to volume), Foundry external revenue reaches tens of billions, DCAI holds share as AI inference pulls general-purpose compute, Nvidia x86+NVLink products ship. Revenue ~2.5x to ~153bn by FY2036 with 50% EBITDA margins (Intel's own pre-2021 level) and capex held at 20-21% to fund it. Higher cap multiple (15x) for a structurally growing leading-edge foundry.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (Foundry's external customer base is still ~0.4bn/qtr against ~100bn of PP&E, and management has itself said 14A is contingent on a major external customer) and the Q4-2026 guide cut shows limited visibility. Base held at 50% as the most likely path given 18A is shipping on schedule and DCAI is supply-constrained. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: a 14A anchor customer, sustained DCAI share against AMD and custom silicon, and margin recovery to pre-2021 levels.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
